travelGuidelines.title: Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) Entry Formalities
travelGuidelines.desc: Domestic travelers only require valid National ID cards at Army checkpoints in Khagrachari, Sajek, and Bandarban. Foreign passport holders require prior security clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs (or on-spot foreign registration at Bandarban / Khagrachari DC offices). Always carry multiple paper photocopies of your passport, visa, and entry stamps.

travelGuidelines.title: Mobile Connectivity & Internet in Remote Areas
travelGuidelines.desc: Grameenphone and Teletalk offer the strongest coverage in remote hill tracts (Sajek, Keokradong, Bandarban) and mangrove forests (Sundarbans). In central haor waters, Robi and GP both perform reliably. Buy a local Tourist SIM at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport arrivals using your passport and biometric fingerprint.

travelGuidelines.title: Cash vs. Mobile Banking (bKash / Nagad)
travelGuidelines.desc: While credit cards (Visa/Mastercard) are accepted in hotels in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Cox's Bazar, remote spots like Sajek, Tanguar Haor, and Birishiri run predominantly on physical cash and bKash / Nagad mobile wallets. Always withdraw sufficient paper currency before departing regional hub towns.

travelGuidelines.title: Cultural Etiquette & Respectful Photography
travelGuidelines.desc: Dress modestly when visiting historic mosques, Hindu temples, Buddhist monasteries, and rural villages (shoulders and knees covered). Always ask polite permission before photographing local village women, fishermen, or indigenous hill residents. Tipping ৳50-100 to helpful boatmen and porters is standard courtesy.

travelGuidelines.title: Leave No Trace & Eco Preservation
travelGuidelines.desc: Help preserve Bangladesh's pristine wonders: strictly avoid dumping single-use plastics into the freshwater of Tanguar Haor, the coral beds of Chera Dwip, or the mangrove streams of the Sundarbans. Always bring your personal trash back to mainland waste disposal bins.
